properties.name: weakcrypto:config
properties.value: skill pq-crypto, 2 scouts, max iterations 400, build bbcd802706e4

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js ships JS implementations of the SHA-1/SHA-2 family inside the buidler/web3 Ethereum toolchain; no direct call site in the challenge code. Hashes face only Grover (square-root), not Shor — low PQ urgency. Same logical dependency as LIB-e966a74e.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js is a transitive toolchain dependency; nothing in the repo's own code calls MD5 and no security function depends on it. MD5 is collision-broken classically — inventoried because the build ships it, not because this repo uses it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Transitive toolchain dependency of the build; no first-party call site. SHA-1 is collision-broken and is inventoried because crypto-js ships it, not because this repo uses it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The secp256k1 npm package (native libsecp256k1 bindings) is the ECDSA transaction-signing core of the buidler/web3 Ethereum dev toolchain that this repo runs its tests with: every web3.eth.sendTransaction in the 8 challenge tests is signed with secp256k1 ECDSA. Quantum-vulnerable under Shor, but the curve is fixed by the Ethereum protocol — observable here, replaceable only by an Ethereum protocol-level migration, not by this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the npm package evp_bytestokey (8 declarations in package-lock.json) implements OpenSSL's EVP_BytesToKey — a single-round MD5-based KDF (the same KDF that is crypto-js's default key derivation). It ships with this build as a transitive dependency of the buidler 1.4.7 / web3 toolchain (crypto-browserify stack); package.json declares no crypto directly. No call site in first-party code (contracts are Solidity; tests use only openzeppelin/chai helpers) — presence is what this

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: bcrypt-pbkdf@^1.0.0 (4 declarations in package-lock.json) ships OpenBSD's bcrypt_pbkdf — a bcrypt-core-based KDF used for encrypted-key files. Transitive dependency of the buidler/web3 toolchain; no direct crypto dependency in package.json; no call site in first-party code. Changeable only by the toolchain maintainers.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: create-ecdh (4 declarations + 1 dep_scan site in package-lock.json) provides ECDH key agreement (the browser shim of Node's crypto.createECDH, supporting secp256k1, X25519, NIST P-curves). Transitive dependency of the buidler/web3 toolchain's crypto-browserify stack; no first-party call site. Quantum-relevant as classical key agreement, but unused in the application's own code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl@0.14.5 provides Ed25519 signatures (nacl.sign). Declared in package-lock.json as a transitive dependency of the buidler toolchain; no call site in first-party code — the application's contracts authenticate via Ethereum's protocol-level secp256k1, not Ed25519. Quantum-unsafe signature capability present in the shipped build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic provides pure-JS ECDSA/ECDH over secp256k1 and other curves to the browserify-sign/create-ecdh layers and the Ethereum toolchain inside this build; no direct call site in the repo's own 10 JS or 19 Solidity files. Same logical dependency as LIB-a0bfbc1a (package-level view).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl@0.14.5 provides X25519 (Curve25519) scalar multiplication (nacl.scalarMult) for key agreement. Transitive dependency in package-lock.json; no first-party call site. Classical key agreement capability shipped in the build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: These packages supply the Keccak-256 hashing used throughout the Ethereum toolchain (transaction and address derivation). The repo's first-party counterpart — explicit keccak256 calls in the challenge contracts for AccessControl role IDs — is reported separately as a finding. Hash primitive: Grover-only exposure, no Shor risk.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: scrypt-family packages — scrypt@^6.0.2 (native), scrypt-js 2.x/3.x, js-scrypt, scrypt.js, scrypt-shim and @web3-js/scrypt-shim (github-pinned) — 24 declarations in package-lock.json. These ship the scrypt KDF (memory-hard password derivation; in Ethereum tooling, scrypt derives keystore-file encryption keys). All transitive dependencies of the buidler/web3 toolchain; no first-party call site. Every one of the 24 sites seen is a lockfile declaration of a scrypt package.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 is required by ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3 (package-lock.json:2371) for the web3 keystore/account-encryption key-derivation layer of the buidler dev toolchain. No application call site; iteration count and parameters are chosen by the toolchain, not by this repo. Same logical dependency as LIB-ea49d4c1.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: crypto-js@3.3.0 (declared in package-lock.json, transitive) ships AES (default CBC with EVP_BytesToKey-derived keys when used with passphrases), plus the SHA family, HMAC, PBKDF2 and MD5. No first-party call site — package.json declares no crypto directly and no require('crypto-js') exists in the repo. The library is unmaintained upstream (4.x frozen), which is a patchability concern, not an algorithm-inventory one.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: tweetnacl@0.14.5's nacl.secretbox implements XSalsa20-Poly1305 authenticated encryption. Transitive dependency declared in package-lock.json; no first-party call site. Note crypto-js and tweetnacl are unmaintained upstream, which matters for patchability, not for the algorithm inventory itself.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider inventory: tweetnacl@0.14.5, declared in package-lock.json (2 sites: root declaration + lockfile), is the provider behind the Ed25519 (ALG-683d5cd2), X25519 (ALG-defedad1) and XSalsa20-Poly1305 (ALG-f58a8f00) algorithm objects — those are this library's shipped capabilities, decomposed by the collector for the CBOM. Transitive dependency of the buidler 1.4.7 toolchain; no first-party call site (the application authenticates via Ethereum protocol secp256k1, not tweetnacl). Unmaint

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider inventory: crypto-js@3.3.0, declared in package-lock.json (2 sites), is the provider behind the AES (ALG-0eb2c0da) and part of the EVP_BytesToKey (ALG-97a780a0) objects — its shipped algorithm surface (AES, SHA-1/SHA-2, HMAC, PBKDF2, MD5, RC4-drop) enters the build through this declaration. Transitive dependency; no first-party call site. Unmaintained upstream, so patchability of anything that does call it would depend on this pinned 3.3.0 version.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt memory-hard KDF used by the Ethereum keystore-encryption layer of the buidler/web3 toolchain; no direct call in the repo's own code. scrypt is a KDF with no Shor exposure, but its cost parameters live in the toolchain, not here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js provides streamable SHA-1/SHA-256/SHA-512 to the browserify/create-hash layer inside the buidler/web3 Ethereum toolchain; no direct call site in the repo's own code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Library presence is the inventory question here: elliptic ships ECDSA-on-secp256k1 code to any code that requires it, whether or not this application calls it; no application call site found in first-party code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.3 provides SHA-1/SHA-2 hashing primitives to the Ethereum toolchain; dependency shipped in the build, no first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2@3.0.17 ships the PBKDF2-HMAC key-derivation primitive to the Ethereum toolchain's account-encryption layer; dependency shipped in the build, no first-party call site.
